summary: Remote route stitch caused repeated cross-region TCP handoffs and inference timeout bursts
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-10 05:12 UTC, a subset of inference requests from FocusDocs' enterprise account experienced spikes in tail latency (p95/p99) and intermittent 504 timeouts. Spikes correlated with a small percentage (~3-5%) of requests being routed through an unintended remote POP and then immediately stitched back to the original region, producing duplicate TCP flows and retransmits. Impact: Customer-facing production traffic saw elevated completion failures for streaming responses and full-response timeouts for synchronous calls. Reported by customer monitoring (increased error rate) and platform telemetry (p95 jump from ~400ms to 2.5s, p99 to 6s). Environment: Production, multi-region deployment for FocusDocs account with geo-affinity enabled and custom route-weights.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Replayed sampled request IDs from affected window via internal replay tool (trace IDs: 20260310-FD-*. See logs). 2) Observed routing decisions in routing-service logs for the account. 3) Captured tcpdump on edge-proxy and on downstream POP for a single request that experienced stitch. Observed behavior: 1) Initial SYN/handshake to local POP A (us-east-1). 2) Proxy config triggered a route-stitch to POP B (ap-southeast-1) mid-session due to a late policy evaluation that returned a higher-weight fallback. 3) The connection manager attempted a hot-handoff by opening a second upstream connection to POP B while the first connection was still active to POP A. This created duplicated in-flight state and packet retransmits; downstream serving-runtime experienced KV cache misses and increased latency as requests were retried. Expected behavior: Routing decisions should be stable per-request (no mid-session region handoff), or handoff should gracefully drain prior connection without duplicating active requests.

Logs / telemetry snippets: - routing-service log (2026-03-10T05:12:23Z): account=focusdocs route_eval_id=rv-2384 weight_delta=+0.12 policy_eval_stage=late - edge-proxy tcpdump (us-east-1): duplicate SYN/ACK to target POPs within 80ms window; retransmit rate +240% - serving-runtime traces: request_id=20260310-FD-721 latency_ms=6120 model=redwood-rlhf-7b-v2 kv_cache_miss=true - console dashboard link: /dashboards/tenant/focusdocs/latency/2026-03-10

Investigation notes: - Root cause: a recently deployed routing optimization (PR 482) introduced a late policy recalculation for accounts with per-tenant dynamic weights. For low-volume catchpaths, the policy recalculation could flip the preferred POP after initial connection selection, triggering the proxy hot-handoff path. The hot-handoff code path was not idempotent for in-flight streaming, so streaming frames were duplicated or dropped during the switch. - Repro: Deterministic when route weights for an account changed during the request lifetime (e.g., near real-time quota enforcement triggered weight adjustments). Replayed test with artificially toggled weight change reproduced p99 spike. - Scope: ~0.8% of overall platform requests during the window, concentrated to accounts using custom route weights; FocusDocs hit impactful error rates due to heavy streaming usage.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-10 06:03 UTC): - Disabled late policy recalculation for sticky-account routing via config flip (feature-flag: routing-late-recalc -> off) at edge fleet. This prevented further mid-session handoffs. - Enabled connection-draining throttle on proxy to avoid opening new upstream connections until ongoing streams complete. Effect: error rate returned to baseline within ~15 minutes; p99 back to ~450ms.

Permanent fix deployed (2026-03-11 22:10 UTC): - Rollback of the late-recalc behavior and a small code change in proxy hot-handoff to ensure per-request pinning and graceful drain path (PR 495). - Added additional test coverage for streaming handoff and added telemetry metric that counts mid-session region changes per-request. - Post-deploy validation run against FocusDocs traffic replay confirmed no duplicates and normalized latency.

Resolution: Root cause identified and fix rolled out to prod; customer notified and incident marked resolved. Post-incident actions assigned.

Follow-up actions: 1) Create a runbook section for mid-session handoffs and add an automated alert (routing.mid_session_handoff_rate > 0.1%) - owner: SRE. 2) Backfill end-to-end tests for streaming handoff scenarios in CI - owner: infra-team. 3) Review per-tenant weight mutation windows and add rate limiter to weight changes to avoid policy flips during active requests - owner: routing team. 4) Outreach to FocusDocs CS to offer postmortem and credit for the impacted window.
comments: 2026-03-10 05:45 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer reported repeated streaming disconnects and 504s. Collected sample request IDs and confirmed platform-side p99 spike. Escalated to SRE and Routing.

2026-03-10 06:05 UTC — SRE (Liam): Flipped routing-late-recalc feature-flag off across edge fleet as an emergency mitigation. Noted p99 improvement in telemetry. Continuing investigation into policy code path.

2026-03-10 12:30 UTC — Routing Eng (Sofia Martinez): Identified PR 482 as introducing late policy recalculation. Repro confirmed via replay with dynamic weight toggles. Preparing code fix and additional tests.

2026-03-11 22:20 UTC — Release Eng (Liam): Deployed patch PR 495 to prod, validated through replay and targeted canary with FocusDocs. No further handoffs observed. Marking incident resolved pending postmortem.
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC — Customer Success (Ethan Park): Notified FocusDocs with summary, provided temporary credits, and scheduled follow-up postmortem call. Customer confirmed resumed normal service.
Postmortem note: Add routing.mid_session_handoff_rate alert and add CI tests for streaming handoff path. Assigned to routing and infra owners with 2-week due dates.
